Lark's comprehensive and in-depth open capabilities serve as a hub of information and an entry point for businesses, integrating with existing IT ecosystems in enterprises. It effectively supports and complements existing IT systems, enhances digital efficiency in enterprises, and assists in building an all-in-one collaborative platform, allowing employees to focus on their work and simplifying their tasks, while enabling IT personnel to develop agilely and enjoy a better user experience. Integrating enterprise systems with the Lark Open Platform can quickly break down barriers between systems and facilitate more efficient information transmission. Enterprises can utilize multiple Lark module capabilities such as documents, address books, messages, and user cards in both existing and new applications, enabling efficient collaboration beyond Lark. We provide diverse integration solutions for enterprises to meet their customization needs and address complex business scenarios. We support integration with CRM, OA, ERP, finance, and other systems, helping bridge the gap between business systems and users, and empowering enterprises to achieve digital transformation. Use Cases Efficient business message circulation with "bots + message cards" Lark bots can be integrated with Lark Calendar, Approval, Cloud Documents, third-party mainstream business systems, and enterprise-built systems. By sending message cards to users, various types of application notifications and alerts can be aggregated in Lark. For example, it can integrate with existing business systems in an enterprise to send monitoring alerts, reminders for to-do tasks, company event notifications, daily data reports, stock alerts, and more. Message cards are a type of message that can contain rich text content and interactive functions. With message cards, you can: Use the rich text styles and graphic layout modules provided by message cards to send visually appealing cards, such as eye-catching notifications and articles with images, ensuring important information reaches users effectively. Use the interactive components provided by message cards to allow users to perform system operations such as approval, voting, and alert handling directly in the chat session without leaving Lark. Fullscreen Exit fullscreen Play Pause 00:00 00:00 2x 1.5x 1x 0.75x 0.5x 1x Pop-out Replay To help developers visualize the completion of message cards, we provide a Message Card Builder tool. It allows for easy drag-and-drop addition of module components, providing a smooth experience. The tool also offers a rich library of card templates, including templates for various scenarios, enabling one-click activation for convenient and efficient use. Rich open capabilities and components that support diverse integration needs of enterprises Enterprises can call multiple Lark module capabilities, including Lark Docs, multidimensional spreadsheets, address books, messages, tasks, user cards, and more, in their existing systems and new applications. The opened and supported capabilities can be found in the " Open Capability List " on the Open Platform official website . In addition to the extensive server API , Lark also provides the ability to develop various types of applications to suit customized needs. An Lark application is a carrier for developers to provide services to their users. It is usually presented in the form of bots, webapps, gadgets , etc. It also has access to the full scope of the platform, paving the way for more enhanced, custom, and powerful experiences within Lark. Some tips on makeing the choices: Bots: interact with users in chat, retrieve data, send/respond to messages, access Lark OpenAPIs Webapp : frequent content updates, existing h5 app migration Gadgets/miniapp : complex modules, require phone/Lark functions, native and smooth user experience The various applications commonly seen in the Workbench are Lark gadgets or Lark web applications, such as approval, and Lark Help Center. Lark can integrate various types of applications: App Type Bot H5 Workbench Block Gadget Demo Applicable Scenarios Applications that interact with users in chat, automatically send messages to users or groups, respond to users' messages and manage groups. Quickly integrate existing web applications, then users can quickly access them without logging. Add data charts, text and pictures and other information to the workbench. Apps that can run in the Lark client and call Lark components to achieve a native-level experience. Dev Tools Purely server-side development, with Message Card Builder provided Lark Developer Tools IDE Lark Developer Tools IDE Lark Developer Tools IDE Dev Resources Develop a bot H5 JS API Block introduction Components & APIs For more information, refer to the Introduction to Application Capabilities . Services and Support Obtain Technical Support : Click the technical support button at the bottom right of any page on the official website to consult any questions you encounter during development. Technical professionals will assist you one-on-one to solve your problems. Provide Feedback on Document Issues : If you discover any errors in the development documentation, you can directly provide feedback by selecting the text on the document page. The feedback will be sent directly to the document authors, and you will receive notifications from Lark once the issue is resolved. Get updates on Lark's open capabilities : Explore newly released capabilities: Changelog Join the developer community : If you want to have access to the latest capabilities for beta testing and connect with other enterprise developers, feel free to join the Lark Developer Community . Reach a whole new world of Message Cards, with the newly updated Message Card Builder ! Important Lark CLI is now open source Empower your workflow with the open-source Lark CLI. Access and manage 12 business domains — including IM, Drive, Base, Calendar, and Meetings — directly from your agents. Licensed under MIT. Get started with a single command: npx @larksuite/cli@latest install Get started | GitHub | Feature wishlist October 12, 2026 AI Lark CLI Weekly Update (September 28-October 4) This release adds approval handoffs for Miaoda app releases and lets you read message content from files or standard input. It also improves calendar card output, authorization guidance, API error messages, and Drive folder moves. Miaoda Submit app releases for approval : Frontend and full-stack apps require a confirmed reason via --apply-reason : a single non-empty line (max 1,000 characters). Skip this flag for creative-mode HTML apps. When approval is pending, the Agent stops polling and presents a valid approval link if available. After you confirm the approver has acted, it rechecks the same release and reports deployment complete only when the status is finished . Use lark-cli apps +release-create and lark-cli apps +release-get . Distinguish database approval from file errors : If publishing database changes requires approval, the CLI directs you to the app release flow or web console. You can still preview pending database changes. File operations distinguish a malformed app ID, a missing app, and insufficient permissions, avoiding repeated environment changes or reauthorization. Use lark-cli apps +db-env-migrate , lark-cli apps +db-env-diff , and lark-cli apps +file-get . Messages and calendar events Read message content from files or standard input : When sending, replying to, or editing a message, --text , --markdown , and --content accept @./path for a local file or - for standard input. This lets you reuse a saved draft or pipe output from another command. Escape a literal leading @ with @@ . Use lark-cli im +messages-send , lark-cli im +messages-reply , and lark-cli im +messages-edit . Find events from calendar cards : Calendar invitations and cards in chat retain open_calendar_id , open_event_id , and share_token in the output when those fields are present in the original message, allowing an Agent to look up the corresponding event. Use lark-cli im +chat-messages-list . Sign-in and authorization Preserve security policy guidance : When a security policy blocks sign-in, credential retrieval, or identity verification, the CLI now preserves the server message, verification link, and rule details. Device authorization polling no longer retries these blocks as network errors. Successful app credential requests also pass the server's status message to the Agent. Use lark-cli auth login and lark-cli auth status --verify . Error messages Show specific API error messages : When an OpenAPI response includes a detailed error message, the CLI displays it instead of the generic message. If no detailed message is available, it uses the generic message. Error codes and classifications remain unchanged, and permission errors retain the existing authorization guidance. Drive Recognize completed folder moves : If a folder move completes synchronously and the server returns no task ID, the CLI reports success instead of raising a missing-task-ID error. If the server returns a task ID, the CLI continues checking the asynchronous task. Use lark-cli drive +move . Get started: Run lark-cli update to upgrade an existing installation. For a first-time installation, run npx @larksuite/cli@latest install . Learn more: Onboarding Guide | GitHub | Feature Requests September 21, 2026 AI Lark CLI Weekly Update (September 14-20) This release adds Miaoda app source export and NPS dashboard blocks for Base. It also improves how Lark Sheets determines write ranges, resolves sheet selectors, and recognizes parameter variants. Miaoda Export app source code : Download a Miaoda app's source code as a zip archive for reading, auditing, or archiving. Pass exactly one of --app-id or --meta-token ; use the last path segment of the app's share link as the meta token. --output takes a relative path in the current directory and defaults to <app_id>.zip . The archive contains the app's most recent commit, so uncommitted sandbox changes are not included, and an unpublished app is reported as not published. Use lark-cli apps +export . Base Add NPS blocks to a dashboard : Create an nps block from a table and a single rating field group. category_range sets the three segments as [min, detractor max, passive max, max] , and its first and last values must match the rating field's range. Use lark-cli base +dashboard-block-create --type nps . Lark Sheets Determine the write range from the payload : +cells-set reads the top-left cell of --range as the anchor and extends the write to the row and column count in --cells . A payload larger than the stated range is no longer rejected, and a resized range is reported with the direction of the change and what was written. --start-cell works as an alias for the anchor. In --writes , the top-level sheet selector applies to entries that do not specify their own sheet. Use lark-cli sheets +cells-set . Resolve the target sheet automatically : When neither --sheet-id nor --sheet-name is set, the CLI looks up the workbook at execution time. A workbook with one sheet uses that sheet, and a workbook with several lists the available names in the error. --dry-run and +batch-update sub-operations still require an explicit selector. Use lark-cli sheets +cells-get and lark-cli sheets +cells-set . Accept more parameter spellings and JSON syntax : A flag name that differs only in separators or casing, such as --sheetName or --sheet.name , resolves to the canonical flag, and a flag that belongs to another command points to that command. Non-standard JSON such as single quotes, trailing commas, and unquoted keys is repaired before parsing. Border, font, and dimension values are read in their common vocabularies. A payload with unmatched brackets or a truncated body is still rejected rather than repaired by guesswork. Use lark-cli sheets +cells-set , lark-cli sheets +table-put , and lark-cli sheets +cond-format-create . Video meetings Join and leave meetings as an app bot : +meeting-join and +meeting-leave accept --as bot only, and user identity is no longer supported. The app bot requirement that previously applied to --action start now applies to all operations for both commands. Use lark-cli vc +meeting-join --as bot and lark-cli vc +meeting-leave --as bot . Minutes Sort search results by creation time : Minutes search returns the newest results first and maintains a consistent order across repeated queries and pages. Use lark-cli minutes +search . Get started: Run lark-cli update if Lark CLI is already installed. For a first-time installation, run npx @larksuite/cli@latest install . Learn more: Onboarding Guide | GitHub | Feature Requests September 15, 2026 AI Lark CLI Weekly Update (September 7-13) This release adds tools for managing mail threads and configuring AI classification and analysis in Base workflows. It also improves chat history retrieval, meeting search, and document creation. Mail Manage mail threads in batches : Add or remove labels, move threads to a folder, or move them to the trash. The CLI splits requests involving more than 20 threads into batches. To move threads to the trash, you must confirm the action and pass --yes . Use lark-cli mail +thread-modify and lark-cli mail +thread-trash . Manage incoming mail rules : Automatically archive mail, mark it as read, or move it to a folder based on conditions such as sender, subject, or attachments. View, enable, disable, and reorder rules. You must confirm the action and pass --yes when creating, updating, or deleting a rule. Use lark-cli mail +rule-create , lark-cli mail +rule-update , and lark-cli mail +rule-reorder . Base Classify and analyze data in workflows : Route content to different steps with AI classification branches. Add AI analysis steps with a specified task, table scope, and data access identity. Subsequent steps can use the analysis result. Use lark-cli base +workflow-create and lark-cli base +workflow-update . Set form question order and visibility : Submit the complete ordered list of question IDs to reorder existing questions. Omitted questions are hidden without deleting the underlying fields or data. Use lark-cli base +view-set-visible-fields . Chat history Compact chat and thread output : Read chat history and thread replies as compact Markdown for use as Agent context. This mode cannot be combined with --format , --json , or --jq . Use lark-cli im +chat-messages-list --concise and lark-cli im +threads-messages-list --concise . View folder contents in messages : View the first level of files and subfolders when reading a folder message. Names and file identifiers help locate files to download. Nested folders are not expanded recursively. Use lark-cli im +chat-messages-list . Video meetings Search meetings as an app bot : Find meeting records by keyword, time range, participant, organizer, or meeting room. Provide at least one filter. Results remain subject to the identity's permissions. Use lark-cli vc +search --as bot . Docs and Slides Wait for document creation : When document creation returns an asynchronous task, the CLI checks its status and returns the document result on success. No manual polling is needed. Use lark-cli docs +create . **Page checks ** when writing Slides : Creating or editing slides enables server-side page checks by default. A failed check rejects the write. Pass --no-lint only when you have confirmed that the check should be skipped. Use lark-cli slides +create and lark-cli slides +update-slide . Lark Sheets Preserve row-level chart data points : Disable aggregation when creating or updating a chart. Records with the same category remain separate data points. Use lark-cli sheets +chart-create-basic --aggregate-categories=false and lark-cli sheets +chart-config-update --aggregate-categories=false . Get started: Run lark-cli update if Lark CLI is already installed. For a first-time installation, run npx @larksuite/cli@latest install . Learn more: Onboarding Guide | GitHub | Feature Requests September 8, 2026 AI Lark CLI Weekly Update (August 31–September 6) This release adds attendee details for Calendar events, OKR comment management, and ranking blocks for Base dashboards. It also improves data input in Lark Sheets, command migration, and local file handling. Calendar attendee details List event attendees by type : View the users, meeting rooms, chats, and third-party email addresses associated with an event. Filter attendees by type and paginate through the full list. For chat attendees, the response does not include chat-level RSVP status. Use lark-cli calendar +list-attendees . OKR comment collaboration Review all comments in an OKR cycle : Collect comments on the cycle, Objectives, Key Results, and progress updates, grouped by target and thread in chronological order. You can also paginate through comments for an individual target or retrieve a single comment, using lark-cli okr +comment-detail , lark-cli okr +comment-list , and lark-cli okr +comment-get Create and manage OKR comment threads : Create entity-level comments or replies for cycles and progress updates, or create selected-text comments and replies for Objectives and Key Results. You can update, resolve, reopen, or permanently delete comments. Write and status-change operations require a user identity, using lark-cli okr +comment-create , lark-cli okr +comment-patch , lark-cli okr +comment-solve , lark-cli okr +comment-reopen , and lark-cli okr +comment-delete Ranking blocks in Base dashboards Create ranking blocks : Create or update a Top N ranking with one grouping dimension and one metric, with value-based sorting and optional filters. Top N supports 1–500 items; new blocks default to 10 items in descending value order, using lark-cli base +dashboard-block-create --type ranking and lark-cli base +dashboard-block-update Lark Sheets data input and command migration Write DataFrame-structured data and CSV files directly : Pass dtypes and formats as positional arrays when they align 1:1 with columns , or provide a CSV path with --file . Required flags are now labeled in help, and style validation provides concise, actionable fixes, using lark-cli sheets +table-put and lark-cli sheets +csv-put Migrate legacy scripts to the current Lark Sheets commands : Legacy shortcut aliases have been removed. Update scripts to use commands organized by workbook, sheet, cell, and table operations, such as lark-cli sheets +workbook-create , lark-cli sheets +sheet-create , lark-cli sheets +cells-get , and lark-cli sheets +cells-set . Run lark-cli sheets --help to view the complete command set Local files and Docs media Use absolute paths in approved local directories : Local file flags now accept absolute paths within the working directory and /tmp , as well as ~/files for non-root users. System and common credential directories remain blocked, and relative paths cannot resolve outside the current working directory. This applies to local-file commands such as lark-cli docs +media-insert and lark-cli im +messages-resources-download Upload media to Word files in Lark : When the target is a Word file stored in Lark, the CLI automatically selects the Office media mount point, so you do not need to switch the underlying parent type manually, using lark-cli docs +media-upload Get started : Run lark-cli update if Lark CLI is already installed. For a first-time installation, run npx @larksuite/cli@latest install . Learn more : Onboarding Guide | GitHub | Feature Requests September 1, 2026 AI Lark CLI Weekly Update (August 24–30) This release expands app-bot controls for live meetings and Calendar workflows. It also adds LLM-powered Base field extensions, richer chart and conditional-format workflows in Lark Sheets, and new tools for rich-text messaging and content management. Live-meeting control and Calendar workflows Join and control live meetings through an app bot : Use an app bot to join or start a meeting from a Calendar event and invite up to 200 specified users or eligible attendees. In the same workflow, capture screenshots, run a countdown, and end the meeting when the app bot is the host.
